title: HTTP /deployments/health/read serves environment state, the last error line and the open incident, composed into the production listener
description:
PREREQUISITE row filed by architect-fa3a3e17 on 2026-09-06 while planning task-85895a88a2484d8589046b2030efd445 (the Needs-you incident card), which cannot read anything without it. Grandchild A task-df972c274f2a4 (the Environments surface, order 123.1) needs the SAME read, so this row serves both and is filed once rather than twice.

THE GAP, MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04):
- `ls apps/daemon/src/http/ | grep -i incident` returns NOTHING. No deployment-health or incident route exists.
- `/health/read` EXISTS and is NOT this. apps/daemon/src/http/health-read.ts (217 lines) is mounted (daemon-store-foundation-composition.ts:51) and proxy-pinned (dev-proxy-paths.ts:24), but its `HealthView` (:51) covers PROVIDER PAUSE and REPOSITORY RESERVATION - the DAEMON's own health. It is not deployment environment health and the two must not be conflated: overloading it would make one route mean two unrelated things and would put an environment outage behind a daemon-liveness code.
- The durable incident and the probe ring are task-6ec875f4dd5f4f2ab97e46f71bf57b2b's (order 121, its grandchild B task-cc05c473 writes `moe-health-probe/1`, the bounded 1440 ring, the derived UP/DEGRADED/DOWN and the one-open-incident lifecycle). That row is explicitly forbidden from touching any UI, and it writes a DURABLE RECORD with no HTTP surface. This row is the operator-facing read over it.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: `/deployments/health/read` serving, per environment, the DERIVED state (UP / DEGRADED / DOWN), the last probe with its timestamp and latency, THE LAST ERROR LINE VERBATIM, the open incident if any with when it opened, and the PREVIOUS DEPLOY RECEIPT's sha so a consumer can name a rollback target - plus its composition into the PRODUCTION listener, in the SAME row.

DO NOT REPEAT THE DESIGN-READ SPLIT: task-7ca9dca3 served /design/read and task-eb2bb09d then had to exist purely to compose the port into the listener, because a served route nothing mounts satisfies every existence grep while the feature does not exist. The pattern to follow is apps/daemon/src/http/design-read.ts with its .js bridge and test, composed through http-listener-read-dispatch.ts, http-listener.ts, http-listener-guards.ts and daemon-entry.ts.

THE LAST ERROR LINE IS THE POINT. The consuming card's whole reason for existing is that an operator under time pressure should not have to open the logs; a read that returns "unhealthy" instead of the actual error line makes that card useless. Carry the probe's recorded error text verbatim.

THE STATE IS DERIVED, NEVER STORED (that row's rail 4). This read RE-DERIVES from the ring or calls that row's derivation; it must not add a stored status field, which would become a second source of truth that can disagree with its own history.
definitionOfDone: `/deployments/health/read` serves, per environment: the derived state (UP / DEGRADED / DOWN), the last probe (timestamp and latencyMs), THE LAST ERROR LINE VERBATIM, the open incident with its opened-at when one exists, and the previous deploy receipt's sha. Built from the EXISTING probe ring and incident records - it reimplements no derivation and adds NO stored status field. Assert the reuse with a grep in the completion record.

THE LAST ERROR LINE IS VERBATIM, asserted as its own arm: seed a probe failure with a distinctive error text and assert that exact string is what the route returns - not a summary, not a truncation, not a code. A read that returns 'unhealthy' makes the incident card it feeds useless, which is the whole reason this route exists.

THE ROUTE IS COMPOSED INTO THE PRODUCTION LISTENER IN THIS SAME ROW - http-listener-read-dispatch.ts, http-listener.ts / http-listener-guards.ts and daemon-entry.ts, following the design-read precedent. Assert it is reachable from the COMPOSED production listener, not only from a hand-built test server: a served route nothing mounts is exactly why task-eb2bb09d had to exist after task-7ca9dca3.

AN ENVIRONMENT THAT CANNOT BE PROBED IS NEVER REPORTED UP - it carries the probe row's PROBE_URL_MISSING outcome with its code AND layer. Assert the state is not UP, not merely that a refusal member is present.
The response decoder contract is EXACT-KEY: an unknown key and a missing key each refuse with the specific code AND the layer that refused, never merely that decoding failed.

It is DISTINCT from /health/read and does not touch it: apps/daemon/src/http/health-read.ts serves daemon provider-pause and repository-reservation state, and `git status --porcelain` proves that file is untouched. Two unrelated meanings behind one route is a rejection.

Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`. Root `pnpm test` covers no apps/** file, so say that rather than quoting a bare root count line.
taskRails: SERVE AND COMPOSE IN THE SAME ROW. A route that is served but not mounted is the failure that forced task-eb2bb09d to exist after task-7ca9dca3.
THE LAST ERROR LINE IS CARRIED VERBATIM. Summarising it defeats the card this read exists to feed.
THE STATE IS DERIVED, NEVER STORED. Re-derive from the ring or call the probe row's derivation; a stored status field is a second source of truth that can disagree with its own history.
DO NOT OVERLOAD /health/read. It serves the DAEMON's health (provider pause, repository reservation), not deployment environments. Leave apps/daemon/src/http/health-read.ts untouched.

NO UI, NO PROXY PIN, NO CLIENT DECODER: the control-room half belongs to task-85895a88a2484d8589046b2030efd445 and task-df972c274f2a4, and touching apps/control-room here collides in the shared worktree.
Reuse an already-rostered layer literal; introduce no new `*_LAYER` constant, which would demand a boundary-roster backfill this row does not own.

  - `export const DEPLOYMENTS_HEALTH_READ_PATH = "/deployments/health/read" as const;` (design-read.ts:13)
  - `const LAYER = "…" as const;` MODULE-LOCAL (design-read.ts:14).   - A `refused(code, layer = LAYER)` factory (:29) so no call site can pair a code with the wrong layer.
  - A PORT INTERFACE the module does not construct — `DesignReadPort` (:25) is documented as "Closed over a store by tests and by the composition sibling; this module does not open one." Yours takes the probe/incident reads the same way. This is what lets step 4 mount it and the tests inject it.
  - EXACT-KEY BODY DECODING via `decodeBoundedJsonBytes` then an explicit allowed-keys check (:38-57). Note the header rule at :1-5: `projectId` comes from the AUTHENTICATED PRINCIPAL, and a payload that names it is an UNKNOWN KEY, not a convenience. Keep that.

implementationPlan.note:
ROUTE MODULE LANDED. apps/daemon/src/http/deployments-health-read.ts (251 lines, under the 250 target after two comment trims; hard cap 400) + the one-line bridge apps/daemon/src/http/deployments-health-read.js (`export * from "./deployments-health-read.ts";`, exactly design-read.js's form — without it plain node cannot load the module).

SHAPE, all fields traced to a measured record; nothing invented:
- `DEPLOYMENTS_HEALTH_READ_PATH = "/deployments/health/read"`.
- `DEPLOYMENTS_HEALTH_READ_CODES` frozen closed roster, one member.
- `DeploymentsHealthReadPort.read({environment}) -> HealthProbeResult<DeploymentsHealthSource>` — the PORT INTERFACE the module does not construct, per the design-read/environments-read precedent. `HealthProbeResult` is the probe row's OWN result type, reused, so a store refusal arrives already paired with its code and its `DAEMON_INGRESS` layer.
- `DeploymentsHealthSource = { deploys: EnvironmentDeployState | null, incidents: readonly HealthIncident[], probes: readonly HealthProbe[] }` — deliberately RAW durable material, all three types IMPORTED from their owners (deploy-ledger.js, health-probe-contracts.js). A port that returned a state would move the derivation out of the served path, which is what rail 3 forbids.
- Served view: `{environment, incident, lastError, lastProbe, ok:true, probeRefusal, rollbackSha, state}`. NO STORED STATUS FIELD anywhere (rail 3).

RAIL 3 — DERIVATION REUSED, NOT REIMPLEMENTED. `import { deriveHealthState } from "../monitoring/health-probe-ring.js"` and `state: deriveHealthState(source.probes)` inside `projectDeploymentsHealth`. Grep proof: `grep -n 'deriveHealthState' apps/daemon/src/http/deployments-health-read.ts` -> the import and the single call site; there is no `UP`/`DOWN` comparison or threshold anywhere in the file.

RAIL 2 — THE ERROR LINE IS VERBATIM. `errorLineOf` walks `deploys.receipts` BACKWARDS to the last receipt carrying a refusal and emits `{at: decidedAt, code, layer, line: refusal.detail, source:"DEPLOY_RECEIPT"}`. `line` is `refusal.detail` assigned straight across — no slice, no template, no join, no summariser. The `source` tag exists so a consumer cannot mistake a deploy-time line for a probe-time one; it is a closed one-member union today because DEPLOY_RECEIPT is the only place this domain records error text (step-1 finding 1).

DoD 4 — `probeRefusalOf` returns `{ok:false, code: PROBE_URL_MISSING, layer:"DAEMON_INGRESS"}` when the current receipt is DEPLOYED but names no url. That is exactly `probeEnvironment`'s own condition (health-probe-ring.ts:190-197: it reaches the url check only after `outcome === "DEPLOYED"`, and mints PROBE_URL_MISSING when `receipt.url === null`), and the code literal is IMPORTED from health-probe-contracts.js rather than typed again. Keyed on the RECEIPT, not on a probe row, so an environment with a receipt and no probes yet still reports it. The state cannot be UP in that case because `deriveHealthState` requires a SUCCESS probe and such an environment can never record one.

DoD 5 — EXACT-KEY IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, WITH DISTINCT CODES. `deploymentsHealthReadBodyOf` returns a discriminated result, not null, so unknown and missing are told apart: an unregistered key (including `projectId`) -> LISTENER_DEPLOYMENTS_HEALTH_UNKNOWN_KEY; `environment` absent -> LISTENER_DEPLOYMENTS_HEALTH_MISSING_KEY; undecodable/non-object/empty-or-non-string value -> LISTENER_DEPLOYMENTS_HEALTH_REQUEST_INVALID. environments-read.ts merges the first two into one code; DoD 5 and step 3 item 3 explicitly require them distinguishable, so this route splits them. Layer for all three is the listener's own CONTROL_ROOM_LISTENER, written by `refuseRequest`.

RAIL 6 — NO NEW LAYER LITERAL AT ALL. The module imports `CONTROL_ROOM_LISTENER_LAYER` from http-listener-guards.js (the environments-read.ts:35 precedent) instead of declaring even a module-local `const LAYER`. That satisfies the rail's literal text ("reuse an already-rostered layer literal") more tightly than the plan's suggestion and adds nothing the boundary roster would owe a row. Every other layer in the answer (`DAEMON_INGRESS`, `DAEMON_DEPLOY_ENGINE`) arrives already paired by the module that owns it.

CAPABILITY: GOAL, not ADMIN. `/deployments/read` (repository-workflow-read.ts:33) fences on CAPABILITIES.GOAL and BOOTSTRAP_FAMILY gives every `deployment.*` command GOAL (daemon-command-vocabulary.ts:73-74). environments-read uses ADMIN because it exposes SECRET METADATA; this route exposes none, so matching the deployments read is the consistent choice.

NO SECRET CROSSES THIS BOUNDARY (epic rail 3): the view carries a sha, a state, a timestamp, a latency, an incident id and docker's stderr line. No url, no credential, no variable value, and the module never logs, traces or stringifies a request.

TYPECHECK, run standalone and NOT through a pipe (a piped run reports head's exit code):
  `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json > /tmp/tsc1.txt 2>&1` in apps/daemon -> REA

implementationPlan.description:
RED TESTS FOR THE ROUTE, before composing it.

  1. THE VERBATIM ERROR LINE (DoD 2), and it is this row's reason for existing. Seed a probe failure whose error text is a DISTINCTIVE literal — something no summariser would produce, with punctuation and length — and assert the route returns that EXACT string. Not a substring match, not "contains an error", not a code. Assert equality. The card this feeds exists so an operator under time pressure does not open the logs; a route returning "unhealthy" makes it useless while looking correct.
  2. AN UNPROBEABLE ENVIRONMENT IS NEVER UP (DoD 4). An environment with a deploy receipt but no health URL carries the probe row's PROBE_URL_MISSING outcome with its code AND its layer, and the STATE IS NOT UP. Assert the state — asserting only that a refusal member is present passes for a response that reports UP with a refusal hanging off it.
  3. EXACT-KEY IN BOTH DIRECTIONS (DoD 5): an UNKNOWN key refuses, and a MISSING key refuses, each with the specific code AND the layer that refused. "Decoding failed" is not the assertion — a single generic code for both makes the two indistinguishable to a client.
  4. `projectId` IN THE PAYLOAD IS AN UNKNOWN KEY, not an override. The principal is the authority; assert the refusal rather than assuming it.
  5. THE STATE COMES FROM THE EXISTING DERIVATION (DoD 1). Feed a ring whose derived state would differ from any naive rule over the same latencies, and assert the route returns the DERIVATION's answer. A fixture where both agree proves nothing about which one ran.
  6. NO OPEN INCIDENT is a normal, healthy answer — the incident member is explicitly absent rather than a fabricated empty object.
implementationPlan.note:
ROUTE TESTS LANDED: apps/daemon/src/http/deployments-health-read.test.ts, 20 arms, all green.

GATE, standalone and foreground (no pipe, no chain — a piped run reports tail's exit code):
  `npx vitest run --root . --config package.json src/http/deployments-health-read.test.ts` in apps/daemon
  EXIT=0, and the DISCRIMINATOR count line is present and NONZERO: `Test Files  1 passed (1)` / `Tests  20 passed (20)`. (A missed filter, "No test files found" and "0 passed" are all exit 0; the count line is what a vacuous run never prints.)

THE SIX ARMS THE STEP NAMED, plus what each was hardened against:
1. VERBATIM ERROR LINE (DoD 2). Seeded literal is 178 chars of quoted, punctuated docker output — `failed to solve: process "/bin/sh -c pnpm --filter @acme/api build" did not complete successfully: exit code: 137 (OOMKilled, layer sha256:9f2c1b, 2.4GiB/2GiB)`. Asserted THREE ways: `toEqual` on the whole `lastError` object (with its code DEPLOY_BUILD_FAILED and layer DAEMON_DEPLOY_ENGINE), then `toBe(ERROR_LINE)` byte equality on `.line`, then `toHaveLength(ERROR_LINE.length)`. No `toContain`, no non-emptiness check — a substring assertion passes for a truncation, and truncating is the failure mode that sends the operator back to the logs. A second arm proves the LAST refusal wins over an older one; a third proves null when nothing was refused.
2. UNPROBEABLE IS NEVER UP (DoD 4). Receipt DEPLOYED with `url: null` -> `probeRefusal` toEqual `{code:"PROBE_URL_MISSING", layer:"DAEMON_INGRESS", ok:false}` AND `state` toBe "DEGRADED" plus explicit `not.toBe("UP")`. THE STATE IS ASSERTED, not merely the presence of a refusal member — a response saying UP with a refusal hanging off it would pass the weaker form. Negative control: a receipt that DOES name a url reports `probeRefusal` null.
3+4. EXACT-KEY BOTH DIRECTIONS WITH DISTINCT CODES (DoD 5). Unknown key -> LISTENER_DEPLOYMENTS_HEALTH_UNKNOWN_KEY; missing key -> LISTENER_DEPLOYMENTS_HEALTH_MISSING_KEY; well-formed -> ok. `projectId` in the payload gets its own arm and refuses as an UNKNOWN KEY through the full handler (not just the decoder), so the principal stays the authority. A further arm covers non-object bodies, an empty-string environment and a numeric one -> LISTENER_DEPLOYMENTS_HEALTH_REQUEST_INVALID. The code+layer pairing over the REAL SOCKET is asserted in step 4's composed test, where `refuse()` actually writes the CONTROL_ROOM_LISTENER layer onto the wire body.
5. THE DERIVATION, ON A RING WHERE A NAIVE RULE DISAGREES (DoD 1). `[FAILURE, FAILURE, FAILURE, SUCCESS]` -> the route answers **UP**, because `deriveHealthState` keys on the LAST observation. Any "majority failed", "recent failures" or "latency threshold" rule reimplemented in this route answers DOWN or DEGRADED on that fixture, so it discriminates. Two more divergent fixtures: `[SUCCESS, FAILURE, FAILURE]` -> DEGRADED (a "two strikes" rule would say DOWN) and `[FAILURE x3]` -> DOWN. Each is asserted as a LITERAL and ALSO cross-checked against `deriveHealthState` directly, so a changed derivation and a reimplemented one are both visible. A separate arm feeds the SAME deploy state with two different rings and gets UP then DOWN, pinning that the state tracks history rather than anything stored beside it.
6. NO OPEN INCIDENT IS A NORMAL ANSWER. `incident` is null on an empty list AND on a list holding only a CLOSED incident — the second case is the one that matters: a route returning `incidents.at(-1)` would stay green on the empty list while reporting a resolved outage as current. A fourth case (closed row followed by an open one) proves the OPEN incident is chosen, not the last row.

ALSO COVERED, because they are this route's failure paths and belong in the owning row rather than a separate evidence row: the last probe's timestamp+latency+status and its null-before-first-probe; the rollback sha is the PREVIOUS receipt's and explicitly `not.toBe` the current one; null rollback on a first deploy; the ABSENT PORT refusing LISTENER_DEPLOYMENTS_HEALTH_UNAVAILABLE rather than a healthy default; the capability denial answering 200 with code AND layer CONTROL_ROOM_LISTENER (distinct from the 503, so the two refusal layers are told apart); the store's own PROBE_STORE_UNAVAILABLE forwarded VERBATIM with its DAEMON_INGRESS layer; and an unauthenticated caller refused BEFORE the port is consulted (asserted with a spy flag, so "it refused" cannot be satisfied by the port having answered first).

NOTE ON ORDER. The plan titles this step "RED TESTS ... before composing it", but step 2 already landed the module, so these arms are green on arrival. The red evidence the plan actually wants comes from the step-5 mutation drills, which mutate the PRODUCTION surface and confirm each arm goes red — that is the stronger form and it is where the three named drills live.

The four new LISTENER_* codes are NOT yet in `LISTENER_REFUSAL_CODES`/`statusFor`; that is a step-4 composition edit. Nothing composed yet.

EVIDENCE DETAIL for QA (overflow from completionSummary's 2000-char cap). Part 1 of 2: measurements and the error-line decision.

THE ONE DESIGN DECISION A REVIEWER SHOULD CHECK FIRST — WHERE THE VERBATIM ERROR LINE COMES FROM.
The row's description says "Carry the probe's recorded error text verbatim." Measured at HEAD, THE PROBE ROW RECORDS NO ERROR TEXT AT ALL. apps/daemon/src/monitoring/health-probe-contracts.ts:1 says so in its own words: "Probe observations, not a stored health verdict. No URL, body or exception is persisted." HealthProbe is exactly {version, environment, sha, status, latencyMs, at}; the `health_probes` table columns are (sequence, project_id, environment, version, sha, status, latencyMs, at); `health_incidents` holds (id, project_id, environment, opened_at, closed_at, opening_probes_json). Command run: `grep -rniE 'error|stderr|detail|message' apps/daemon/src/monitoring/*.ts | grep -v '\.test\.'` -> every hit is a thrown PROBE_STORE_UNAVAILABLE or `redirect: "error"`. There is no error-text field to read.
The ONLY verbatim error text this domain records is DeployReceiptV1.refusal.detail, documented at apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-receipt-contracts.ts:34 as "`docker build` refused; the detail carries docker's own last stderr line", carried with its own closed code roster (DEPLOY_REFUSAL_CODES) and its own layer (DEPLOY_ENGINE_STAMP = "DAEMON_DEPLOY_ENGINE").
So the route serves THAT, untouched, as `lastError: {at, code, layer, line, source:"DEPLOY_RECEIPT"}`. The `source` tag is deliberate: it is a one-member union today, and it exists so a consumer cannot mistake a deploy-time line for a probe-time one, and so the probe row can add "HEALTH_PROBE" later without a breaking change. I did NOT invent a probe error field (that would have been a fabricated record shape) and I did NOT summarise (rail 2). If QA judges this the wrong source, the fix is a probe-row change to persist error text, not a change here — this route can only carry what is written.

THE DEPLOY-RECEIPT SHA IS SERVABLE, NOT ABSENT. Step 1 told me to serve it as explicitly absent if task-04b3ce7e had not landed. It HAS: `readPreviousDeployReceipt(store, projectId, environment): DeployReceiptV1 | null` is published at apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-ledger.ts:104 under the heading "THE ROLLBACK TARGET, published as its own call". `rollbackSha` is served for real, from `EnvironmentDeployState.previous.sha`. A test arm asserts it equals the PREVIOUS receipt's sha and `not.toBe` the current one — the ledger walk keeps both and never collapses them.

DoD 1, REUSE PROVED BY GREP. `grep -n 'deriveHealthState' apps/daemon/src/http/deployments-health-read.ts` -> the import at :35 and the single call site at :197 (`state: deriveHealthState(source.probes)`). The counter-grep that matters: `grep -nE '"UP"|"DOWN"|"DEGRADED"|THRESHOLD' apps/daemon/src/http/deployments-health-read.ts` returns NOTHING — no state literal, no threshold, no second derivation anywhere in the route. No stored status field was added; the port hands back RAW material (probes, incidents, deploys) precisely so the derivation stays in the served path.

DoD 6, RE-CHECKED AT THE END. `git status --porcelain -- apps/daemon/src/http/health-read.ts` -> EMPTY. That route still serves only the daemon's provider-pause and repository-reservation state. The two meanings never share a path.

DoD 5, WHY FOUR LISTENER CODES AND NOT THE USUAL TWO. The DoD requires an unknown key and a missing key to be distinguishable. environments-read.ts merges both into one REQUEST_INVALID; this route splits them, so the decoder returns a discriminated result rather than null: LISTENER_DEPLOYMENTS_HEALTH_UNKNOWN_KEY, LISTENER_DEPLOYMENTS_HEALTH_MISSING_KEY, LISTENER_DEPLOYMENTS_HEALTH_REQUEST_INVALID (non-object / undecodable / unusable value / non-POST), LISTENER_DEPLOYMENTS_HEALTH_UNAVAILABLE. All four are in LISTENER_REFUSAL_CODES with statuses (400/400/400/503), and all four are asserted OFF THE WIRE with `layer: "CONTROL_ROOM_LISTENER"`.

RAIL 6 SATISFIED WITHOUT A NEW LITERAL. The plan suggested a module-local `const LAYER`. I instead import the already-rostered CONTROL_ROOM_LISTENER_LAYER (the environments-read.ts:35 precedent), so the boundary roster owes this row nothing at all.

planningNotes.risks:
1. A SERVED-BUT-UNMOUNTED ROUTE. The exact defect that forced task-eb2bb09d to exist after task-7ca9dca3, and it satisfies every existence grep. The tell is a test that builds its own server: it proves the handler works and says nothing about whether the daemon serves it. Drill 1 catches it by removing the daemon-entry wiring.

2. AN ABSENT PORT ANSWERING HEALTHY. The optional-port pattern means a daemon composed without this port must REFUSE AS UNAVAILABLE. If it instead answers a default, every environment reads UP on a daemon that cannot see any of them — the most dangerous possible output from a health route. Drill 3 targets it.

3. THE ERROR LINE SUMMARISED. This route exists so an operator does not open the logs; returning "unhealthy" makes the consuming card useless while the route looks correct. The arm must assert EQUALITY against a distinctive literal, not a substring or non-emptiness.

4. AN UNPROBEABLE ENVIRONMENT REPORTED UP. Asserting only that a refusal member is present passes for a response that says UP with a refusal hanging off it. DoD 4 wants the STATE asserted.

5. RAIL 6 MISREAD AS FORBIDDING A LAYER. It forbids an exported `*_LAYER` constant (a boundary-roster backfill); the precedent uses a module-local `const LAYER`. Read the other way it contradicts DoD 4 and 5 and would stall the row.

6. REIMPLEMENTED DERIVATION. Two opinions about one ring; the browser shows this route's. A fixture where the derivation and a naive rule agree cannot detect it.

7. THE OVERSIZED COMPOSITION FILES being blamed on this diff, or worse, split by it. 557 and 411 are pre-existing; the plan requires noting them and forbids the refactor.
